eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 16 · Writing Data

caption: DELETE removes whole rows -- you can never delete just part of one.

code:
-- Removes EVERY row -- table structure stays, data doesn't
DELETE FROM dbo.LessonDemo;
caption: Columns, constraints, and IDENTITY definition survive -- only the rows are gone.
DELETE is permanent -- look before you act.

code:
DELETE d
FROM dbo.LessonDemo AS d
JOIN Production.Product AS p
    ON d.ProductName = p.Name
WHERE p.ProductLine <> 'R';
caption: The alias goes right after DELETE -- same shape as a joined UPDATE.

subtitle: Two ways to empty a table, and why they differ.
